readerQuestion: Should I use an area or a light group to control several Home Assistant lights together while leaving other lights in the same room alone?
directAnswer: Use areas for physical rooms and eligible whole-room light targets; add a Light Group for a selected fixture or lamp set. Keep the two reading lamps and ceiling in Living room, but select only the lamps in Reading lamps. Start with explicit On/Off and verify the physical lamps. Check hidden-entity filtering and actual member capabilities before relying on area control or dimming.

The decision and troubleshooting tables connect the intended household result to target choice, visibility, member lists and device capabilities.

claimChecks.claim: Areas organize physical rooms and can target their lights; group membership is a separate selection, so a subset can retain its room assignment.
Light Group is created through Helpers; default state is on when any member is on, All entities changes state aggregation, and old-style generic groups are not the recommended new setup.

Version 2026.9.3 area expansion filters hidden and non-primary entities. An explicit group entity can still forward commands to its configured hidden members, so hiding individual controls changes which room targets need verification.

The light-group implementation validates light entities and forwards On/Off to the configured member list. Its aggregate state/capabilities do not confirm every physical bulb changed or grant every bulb the same features.

Light toggle flips based on current state. With default any-on group aggregation, one member on makes a group toggle request Off for the group; explicit On/Off expresses a predictable intended result.
Switch as X can represent an existing lamp switch as a light. It changes entity type, not the physical plug's dimming hardware; the recommendation is limited to an actual lamp plug.
Action targets support entity_id and area_id; the examples are actions, not complete automations or top-level configuration.yaml entries.

Current Tools navigation is Settings > Tools. Actions sends commands; setting a state in States changes Home Assistant's representation rather than controlling the physical device, so verification uses Actions and observation.
A scene can store different desired light states; a shared light group is not a saved individual-state restoration mechanism.
